name: Centro Historico (Ciudad Amarilla)
tagline: The golden heart around the Convento
description: The postcard core of Izamal, where nearly every building is painted golden ochre around the vast Convento de San Antonio de Padua. Walkable plazas, calesas, cafes, and the main market sit within a few blocks, making this the natural base for a short, atmospheric stay.
bestFor: Slow travelers and culture lovers wanting to be in the middle of it all
pros: Cafes, market, and restaurants close by
cons: Modest tourist bustle in peak hours

name: Kinich Kakmo pyramid area
description: A few blocks north of the main square, this quieter pocket sits around the towering Kinich Kakmo pyramid, which you can climb for sweeping views over the yellow rooftops. It blends residential streets with easy access to the town's most impressive Maya monument.
bestFor: History enthusiasts who want the pyramid on their doorstep
pros: Steps from a climbable Maya pyramid

name: Residential barrios (outer Izamal)
description: Beyond the painted core, Izamal's residential barrios are workaday, affordable, and authentically local, with simple homes, corner shops, and little tourism. Renting here means the lowest prices and full immersion in daily Yucatecan life, at the cost of a longer walk to the sights.
bestFor: Budget long-stayers wanting immersion and the cheapest rents
cons: Farther from the sights and cafes
Very little English or tourist infrastructure

name: Merida (larger-services base)
tagline: The regional hub an hour away
description: About an hour west, Merida is where most nomads actually base: a vibrant colonial capital with coworking spaces, a real nomad community, fast internet, hospitals, an airport, and abundant dining and nightlife. Many use it as home and visit Izamal for peaceful cultural day trips or weekends.
bestFor: Nomads needing coworking, community, and city amenities
cons: Not Izamal itself; requires travel to visit
Bigger, busier, and pricier than Izamal
